summary.text: A 70-year-old man with a history of diabetic nephropathy, cerebral infarction and colorectal cancer, undergoing hemodialysis, presented without particular complaints. Four years following hemodialysis he began lanthanum carbonate 1500 mg/day and lansoprazole 30 mg/day. Blood tests showed severe renal impairment during dialysis, elevated magnesium and glycated hemoglobin A1c, and a negative Helicobacter pylori antibody.

Nine years following hemodialysis, screening EGD showed whitish cobblestone-like mucosa in the gastric corpus and reddish depressed lesions with annular whitish mucosa in the antrum, and magnified NBI showed a yellowish–white substance within villous-like structures. Biopsies showed parietal cell hyperplasia and CD68-positive histiocyte aggregates. SEM–EDS detected lanthanum and phosphorus, mainly in histiocytes, confirming lanthanum deposition in the gastric mucosa; retrospective review showed whitish mucosa 6 months after lanthanum began.

Lanthanum carbonate was stopped after the deposition was confirmed and EGD was continued regularly. Three years and 5 months after discontinuation the whitish rough mucosa and depressed lesions improved a little, the white rough mucosa in the gastric body still existed, and histiocyte numbers decreased on follow-up biopsy. The authors plan to continue close monitoring as needed.
